findings.description:
ICE PACK TEST

INDICATION: Evaluation of bilateral ptosis, left greater than right.

TECHNIQUE: Crushed ice in a surgical glove applied over the closed left upper eyelid for 2 minutes. Marginal reflex distance 1 (MRD1) measured immediately before and after application.

RESULTS:
  Left MRD1 before application: 0.5 mm.
  Left MRD1 after application (2 minutes): 3.5 mm.
  Improvement: 3.0 mm.

IMPRESSION: Positive ice pack test (improvement in ptosis of at least 2 mm after cooling). Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Positive ice pack test: left MRD1 improved from 0.5 mm to 3.5 mm (3.0 mm) after 2 minutes of cooling

findings.description: Lobulated, circumscribed mass 4.2 x 3.8 cm; T1 heterogeneous; T2 heterogeneous with areas of high signal (necrosis or cystic change); heterogeneous enhancement; no signal drop on opposed-phase imaging; no restricted diffusion
No pericardial or pleural invasion or nodularity

output.impression: 1. Circumscribed 4.2 x 3.8 cm anterior mediastinal mass with cystic or necrotic areas, no chemical-shift signal drop and no invasion of fat planes, pericardium or pleura: most consistent with a thymoma; thymic carcinoma cannot be excluded. 2. No lymphadenopathy.

findings.description:
BEDSIDE RESPIRATORY FUNCTION TESTING

INDICATION: Generalized fatigable weakness with bulbar symptoms; baseline before thymectomy.

MEASUREMENTS (seated; weight 62.4 kg, height 168 cm):
  FVC: 3.05 L (predicted 3.60 L; 85% predicted; 49 mL/kg)
  MIP (NIF): -52 cmH2O (L; lower limit of normal for age and sex about -60 cmH2O)
  MEP: 68 cmH2O (L; lower limit of normal about 80 cmH2O)
  Single-breath count: 28
  Cough: adequate
  No fall in FVC between seated and supine measurement.

IMPRESSION: 1. Mildly reduced inspiratory and expiratory pressures (MIP -52, MEP 68 cmH2O). 2. FVC preserved (85% predicted, 49 mL/kg). Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Mildly reduced MIP (-52 cmH2O) and MEP (68 cmH2O); FVC preserved at 3.05 L (85% predicted, 49 mL/kg)

action_criteria.expected_evidence: AChR binding antibody 12.4 nmol/L (reference <= 0.02) with blocking 72% and modulating 88%; TSH 1.8 mIU/L, free T4 and anti-TPO normal
action_criteria.label: Order AChR binding antibody and thyroid function
action_criteria.rationale: Fatigable bilateral ptosis, diplopia, bulbar and proximal weakness: AChR binding antibody (RIA or cell-based assay) is the first serological test, with thyroid function for coexisting autoimmune thyroid disease (Evoli, Neurol Sci 2019; Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: 3 Hz decrement in deltoid 18%, nasalis 22% and trapezius 16% with normal baseline CMAPs and no post-exercise facilitation (5%)
action_criteria.label: Order repetitive nerve stimulation at 3 Hz in facial and proximal muscles
action_criteria.rationale: Low-rate RNS of weak facial and proximal muscles documents the postsynaptic decrement, and brief exercise testing excludes the presynaptic facilitation of Lambert-Eaton syndrome (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025; Evoli, Neurol Sci 2019).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Increased jitter in 18 of 20 pairs (mean MCD 88 microseconds) with blocking in 9
action_criteria.label: Single-fibre EMG (not needed once RNS is diagnostic)
action_criteria.rationale: SFEMG is the most sensitive test but is reserved for a normal RNS or seronegative disease; with high AChR titres and a clear decrement it adds nothing to the diagnosis (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left MRD1 improves from 0.5 to 3.5 mm after 2 minutes of ice
action_criteria.label: Bedside ice pack test of the left ptosis
action_criteria.rationale: She has fatigable ptosis, worse on the left; an MRD1 improvement of at least 2 mm after 2-5 minutes of cooling is cheap bedside support for a neuromuscular junction disorder.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Circumscribed 4.2 x 3.8 cm anterior mediastinal mass without invasion, most consistent with thymoma
action_criteria.label: Order contrast CT of the mediastinum for thymoma
action_criteria.rationale: Mediastinal imaging is indicated in every patient with MG to detect thymoma (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025); a thymoma is an indication for resection regardless of MG severity (Sanders 2016).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: MIP -52 and MEP 68 cmH2O mildly reduced; FVC 3.05 L (85% predicted, 49 mL/kg); no crisis threshold met
action_criteria.label: Measure FVC, MIP and MEP before surgery
action_criteria.rationale: Bulbar symptoms and a planned thymectomy: FVC in mL/kg, MIP and MEP stage respiratory muscle strength and set the baseline for anaesthesia and post-operative monitoring (20/30/40 rule, Lawn, Arch Neurol 2001).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Estrogen increases prednisolone exposure; no pyridostigmine interaction; mycophenolate and methotrexate need contraception
action_criteria.label: Check the planned MG treatment against her combined oral contraceptive
action_criteria.rationale: She takes ethinylestradiol/norgestimate; no interaction changes management, but estrogen raises prednisolone exposure and immunosuppressant choice depends on contraception and pregnancy plans.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start high-dose prednisone (above 20 mg/day) as an outpatient; start low and titrate, or start high dose only with inpatient monitoring, because initial steroid-induced worsening can precipitate crisis.

Avoid fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides and IV magnesium unless no alternative exists and the patient is monitored; use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers only at reduced dose with quantitative monitoring.
Do not attribute fatigable ptosis, diplopia or bulbar weakness to a functional or stress-related cause before AChR antibody testing and neurophysiology.
Do not prescribe mycophenolate or methotrexate without effective contraception and pregnancy counselling.
required_recommendations: Refer to thoracic surgery for complete thymectomy with resection of the thymoma: a thymoma is an indication for surgery regardless of MG severity (Sanders 2016), and the 4.2 cm mass needs histology

Optimise MG before surgery because of bulbar weakness: IVIG 2 g/kg (about 125 g over 2-5 days) or plasma exchange pre-operatively, with FVC and MIP rechecked before anaesthesia and the anaesthetist informed (reduced-dose non-depolarising neuromuscular blockade with quantitative monitoring)
Start pyridostigmine 30 mg three times daily and titrate to 60 mg four to five times daily according to response and muscarinic side effects

Start prednisone at 10-20 mg/day and increase gradually with monitoring of bulbar and respiratory function for early steroid-induced worsening; add a steroid-sparing agent (azathioprine after TPMT testing) if long-term steroids are needed

Counsel on pregnancy planning: pyridostigmine, prednisone and azathioprine are acceptable in pregnancy, mycophenolate and methotrexate are teratogenic and need effective contraception and a washout before conception, and a future pregnancy needs joint neurology and obstetric care
Bedside swallow assessment before oral medication and diet changes, given chewing fatigue and dysphagia for pills
Give her a list of drugs that can worsen MG and check every new prescription against it

avoided_actions.rationale: MG is a disorder of the neuromuscular junction; EEG has no diagnostic role (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
CSF has no role in MG and nothing in this presentation raises Miller Fisher syndrome or a CNS cause (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
FDG-PET is not part of the MG or thymoma work-up here; contrast CT (or MRI) of the mediastinum characterises the mass before resection (Jacob, Pract Neurol 2025).
No cardiac symptom or sign, and the CT shows no pericardial involvement; echocardiography adds nothing.
Regular rhythm and no palpitations or syncope; cardiac monitoring is not part of the MG work-up.

accepted: Myasthenia gravis, generalized (MGFA Class IIb-III), AChR antibody-positive, with large thymoma (4.2 cm anterior mediastinal mass)

differential.key_features: Thymic carcinoma is rarely associated with MG; circumscribed margins, preserved fat planes and no lymphadenopathy or pleural deposits on CT and MRI favour thymoma; histology at resection decides.
Normal baseline CMAPs, a 3 Hz decrement and no post-exercise facilitation (5%), preserved reflexes and no autonomic symptoms; AChR binding antibody strongly positive.
No proptosis or lid retraction; ptosis is fatigable and improves with ice; normal TSH, free T4 and anti-TPO.
Markedly elevated AChR antibodies and RNS decrement establish organic pathology.
Subacute 3-month onset, fluctuation, bulbar and limb fatigability and positive AChR antibodies are not compatible with CPEO.

key_clinical_evidence: Fluctuating, fatigable weakness with a diurnal pattern (worse in the evening) is the clinical hallmark of MG; fixed weakness suggests an alternative diagnosis.
Ocular involvement (ptosis, diplopia) is asymmetric and fatigable in MG; thyroid eye disease causes restrictive, not fatigable, ophthalmoplegia.
A high AChR binding titre (12.4 nmol/L) with a 16-22% decrement on 3 Hz RNS establishes generalized AChR-positive MG; SFEMG is not needed.
Mediastinal CT with contrast is indicated in every patient with MG to detect thymoma; here it shows a circumscribed 4.2 cm anterior mediastinal mass most consistent with thymoma.
A thymoma is an indication for thymectomy regardless of MG severity; bulbar weakness calls for pre-operative IVIG or plasma exchange.
Fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides, IV magnesium and neuromuscular blockers can worsen MG and must be checked against every new prescription.

sequence_constraints.reason: Repetitive nerve stimulation is done first; SFEMG follows when RNS is normal (Jacob 2025).
AChR antibody testing precedes single-fibre EMG; SFEMG is reserved for seronegative patients or a normal RNS (Jacob 2025).

findings.density: Heterogeneous soft tissue density with areas of low attenuation
findings.description: Large anterior mediastinal mass. Lobulated borders. Displaces adjacent mediastinal structures but no clear invasion. Contains areas of necrosis or cystic degeneration.

body_imaging.impression: 1. Lobulated, circumscribed anterior mediastinal mass, 4.2 x 3.8 cm, heterogeneous with areas of low attenuation (necrosis or cystic change); fat planes with the great vessels preserved, no invasion. Features most consistent with a thymoma; thymic carcinoma cannot be excluded. 2. No mediastinal lymphadenopathy, pleural effusion or pleural nodularity. 3. Lungs clear.

interactions: PREDNISONE + ETHINYLESTRADIOL: estrogen-containing contraceptives reduce prednisolone clearance and increase its exposure. Moderate. Monitor for corticosteroid adverse effects; no routine dose change.
PYRIDOSTIGMINE + ETHINYLESTRADIOL/NORGESTIMATE: no clinically significant interaction.
prednisone.proposed: prednisone and pyridostigmine; current medication ethinylestradiol 0.035 mg / norgestimate 0.25 mg
warnings: Mycophenolate mofetil and methotrexate are teratogenic: effective contraception is required during treatment and for the washout period before conception.
Azathioprine: check TPMT (or NUDT15) activity before starting; it is not contraindicated in pregnancy.
Combined hormonal contraception with prolonged immobility after surgery: assess venous thromboembolism risk perioperatively.

abnormal_values_summary: AChR binding antibody 12.4 nmol/L (H; reference <= 0.02 nmol/L)
labs.interpretation: AChR binding antibody elevated at 12.4 nmol/L, with elevated blocking (72%) and modulating (88%) antibodies. Blood count, metabolic panel, CK, TSH, free T4 and anti-TPO within reference ranges. Acetylcholine receptor antibodies are found in most patients with generalized autoimmune myasthenia; clinical correlation recommended.

specialized_test.impression: Abnormal RNS: 3 Hz decrement in deltoid 18%, nasalis 22% and trapezius 16% with normal baseline CMAP amplitudes, repair after exercise and post-activation exhaustion; no post-exercise facilitation (5%). Normal nerve conduction studies. Findings are consistent with a postsynaptic disorder of neuromuscular transmission. Clinical correlation recommended.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Three required studies (AChR serology with thyroid function, RNS, mediastinal imaging), thymoma-associated generalized MG with bulbar involvement; management turns on pre-operative optimisation and pregnancy-compatible immunotherapy in a woman on a combined oral contraceptive.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive bilateral ptosis, diplopia, and arm fatigue worse at end of day over 3 months

past_medical_history: No prior neuromuscular or autoimmune disease

patient.history_present_illness: A 34-year-old woman with no significant past medical history presented with a 3-month history of progressive bilateral ptosis, horizontal diplopia, and proximal arm weakness. She first noticed bilateral eyelid drooping approximately 3 months ago, initially only in the evenings. Over time, the ptosis became present throughout the day and progressively worsened, with the left eye more severely affected than the right. She began experiencing double vision when looking to the right, which was intermittent initially but became more frequent. She noticed that her arms became weak and fatigued when blow-drying her hair or reaching for overhead items — she could not maintain her arms elevated for more than 60 seconds. She began having difficulty chewing tough meats by the end of a meal, requiring rest breaks. Her speech became slurred and nasal after prolonged conversation, particularly noticeable in the evenings during dinner. She works as a nurse and noticed she had increasing difficulty performing overhead tasks and her handwriting was becoming affected. She denies any sensory symptoms, no headache, no visual acuity changes, no neck pain, no back pain, no bladder or bowel dysfunction. Her symptoms consistently worsen throughout the day and are significantly better in the morning after sleep. She had a brief visit to urgent care 6 weeks ago where she was told the ptosis was 'stress-related' and given a recommendation to reduce work hours. She has had no recent viral illnesses, no vaccinations, and no new medications. She is otherwise completely healthy. Her mother and aunts have no neuromuscular disease.

neurological_exam.additional: Dysarthria after 3 minutes sustained speech. Mild dysphagia — reports difficulty with pills. No respiratory distress. No stridor.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Bilateral ptosis, left greater than right, MRD1 left 0.5 mm, right 2 mm. Fatigable ptosis on sustained upgaze complete in left eye at 40 seconds. Horizontal diplopia on rightward gaze. Mild limitation of left eye adduction. Pupils equal, 3mm, reactive. No proptosis. Bilateral mild facial weakness.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal casual. Waddling on prolonged walking.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x4. Normal language and cognition.
neurological_exam.motor: Proximal upper extremity weakness: deltoids 4/5 bilaterally, worse on left. Proximal lower extremity: hip flexors 4+/5. Distal strength 5/5. Neck flexors 4/5. Fatigability: deltoid strength drops from 4 to 3/5 after 10 repetitions.

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs; no facial or upper limb venous distension.
physical_exam.general: Alert, well-appearing woman; bilateral ptosis, left greater than right. Weight 62.4 kg, height 168 cm.
physical_exam.respiratory: Clear to auscultation; no accessory muscle use; SpO2 99% on room air.
